summary_en.motivation: To improve the thermal performance of loop heat pipes by optimizing the wick structure using additive manufacturing.
summary_en.method: Wick samples with various designs were fabricated via selective laser melting and assembled into a prototype for testing.
summary_en.result: The optimized wick achieved effective start-up and low thermal resistance in the loop heat pipe.
summary_en.validation: Experimental prototype testing confirmed the wick's thermal performance.

papers.title: Design and integration of a problem-based biofabrication course into an undergraduate biomedical engineering curriculum
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The rapidly evolving discipline of biological and biomedical engineering requires adaptive instructional approaches that teach students to target and solve multi-pronged and ill-structured problems at the cutting edge of scientific research. Here we present a modular approach to designing a lab-based course in the emerging field of biofabrication and biological design, leading to a final capstone design project that requires students to formulate and test a hypothesis using the scientific method. RESULTS: Students were assessed on a range of metrics designed to evaluate the format of the course, the efficacy of the format for teaching new topics and concepts, and the depth of the contribution this course made to students training for biological engineering careers. The evaluation showed that the problem-based format of the course was well suited to teaching students how to use the scientific method to investigate and uncover the fundamental biological design rules that govern the field of biofabrication. CONCLUSIONS: We show that this approach is an efficient and effective method of translating emergent scientific principles from the lab bench to the classroom and training the next generation of biological and biomedical engineers for careers as researchers and industry practicians.

summary_en.motivation: To address the need for adaptive instructional approaches in biomedical engineering by designing a lab-based biofabrication course.
summary_en.method: A modular problem-based course was developed, culminating in a capstone design project requiring hypothesis formulation and testing.
summary_en.result: Student assessments indicated the problem-based format effectively taught fundamental biological design rules and scientific method application.
summary_en.validation: Evaluation relied on student surveys and performance metrics to assess course efficacy.
